HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Romance still, medium shot, low three-quarter angle across a lamplit banquet hall. Maehwa (thirty-one) stands in the foreground under the cheap hanging lamps, one hip cocked, in her old washed-thin green jeogori that clings to her full bust and the narrowest waist in the room, the frayed red sash cinched hard around it, the ochre chima pulled snug over her full curving hips. She holds a ripe blush peach to her lips and sucks it slowly, eyes heavy-lidded and sliding sideways to the top table, a slow knowing half-smile, a line of juice running to her wrist. Deep behind her, out of focus but readable, young Pumsuk (twenty-one, beardless, bare-headed, topknot, ice-blue silk robe) at the top table has gone still with his cup halfway to his mouth, flushed to the ears, staring. ONE device: the peach at her mouth catching the lamp. Sage-green #8AAFA0 on her, ice-blue #7EB8F0 on him. No jougwan, no cap, no feathers on Pumsuk. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = gumilwife, SECOND face = pumsuk. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), binyeo board gumil_wife (her hair ornament exactly; not clothing). MAEHWA — Look: Thirty-one, striking, knowing half-smile, heavy-lidded eyes, dark hair up with a wooden sprig binyeo, loose strands at the neck. The best figure of any woman in the chronicle: tight, curvy hourglass — a tiny waist, full bust and full hips — and she carries it like a weapon; every man in the frame is already looking at her. Dress: Old mended green jeogori washed so thin it clings to her bust and waist, a frayed red sash cinched hard to show how small her waist is, ochre chima pulled snug over her hips (portrait-true). Commoner cloth, no gold — except the gold butterfly once Pumsuk gives it to her. Colour #8AAFA0. KIM PUMSUK — Look: Twenty-one, clean-shaven, smooth boyish handsome face, black hair in a topknot under the Hwarang crescent-moon headband; earnest wide eyes that go startled easily. Dress: Ice-blue silk po belted with a brown sash, dark inner sleeves and wrapped forearms (portrait-true). Colour #7EB8F0. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
